headline: Agentic LLMs are being checked against verifiable biological outcomes in drug workflows
label: Llm Agents For Drug Discovery
summary: Multi-agent and LLM assistants now orchestrate biological tools, so evaluation must test whether their outputs match verifiable results.
synthesis: The common thread across these preprints is the shift from single-task predictive models toward agentic LLM systems that orchestrate external biological tools. OrchestRA links target discovery, pocket-based design, and PBPK pharmacokinetic simulation in an iterative, human-in-the-loop workflow. Alvessa, an evidence-grounded assistant, orchestrates functional genomics tools and checks its statements against retrieved records, directly addressing the verification problem. SpatialBench shifts the evaluation question to whether agents recover key results from 146 verifiable spatial transcriptomics problems. What is new is the emphasis on verifiability: outputs are judged against retrieved evidence or defined biological outcomes rather than solely on predictive accuracy.
